newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas contract sees record low trade volume.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas contract sees record low trade volume.

text.p: The IPE's fledgling natural gas futures contract suffered its worst day yet on Tuesday, with a mere 35 lots traded in six separate deals.
Four deals were struck in the morning, with only two transacted in the afternoon session from 1400 GMT to 1600 GMT.

Brokers were at a loss to explain the lack of interest, although one referred to the "classic Catch-22" of a new contract: there are thought to be several potential players waiting on the wings ready to join in, but until more start playing, they will continue to wait.
There were no technical problems reported on the screen-based trading system, and the lack of trade simply reflected lack of willingness to join in, brokers said.
"We've had little contact with our customers since yesterday," said one, "and they're a little disillusioned about the volumes."

The illiquidity in the market has led to some improbable positions. The closing offer price for March was 11.310 pence a therm, well below the closing bid on April, at 11.60 pence. Normally the two months would be expected to be in backwardation as the weather is warmer in April, but March has been driven so low that they closed firmly in contango.
And the best bid for December by the close was 11.50 pence, lower than the best bid in May at 11.55 pence.

The previous lowest volume of trade was recorded on the second day of the contract, when 40 lots were traded, but the market then suffered from confusion when two deals were busted and there was a system failure in the afternoon. The highest volume of trade was on the first day, January 31, when 465 lots were transacted.
